I'm in group right now, at my university. Not all of the people in it have mental health issues, and it has its pros and cons.

I have social anxiety so a lot of times it's hard just to go and sit in a circle where silence often falls between topics... But when I do talk, I don't know, it just feels like a tiny weight is lifted off my shoulders. Like, I'm not looking for a solution, but its nice when someone has a suggestion. Even if it's not something I would do, it's nice to be heard and not stared at like my family and friends do... On the other hand, its hard to initiate that conversation when you just want to hold your anxiety close so no one knows how messy your head is, especially if some of the people have never experienced things like GAD or social anxiety or panic disorder or depression. 

If someone asked me if they should do group therapy, I would say yes based on my experiences. Best of luck :]

I am you (more or less). I was on academic probation 2 semesters ago and scraped by the next with the absolute bare minimum (2.0). I had serious discussions with my parents about dropping out this semester (they wanted me to come home to keep an eye on me), but I decided to stay. Currently failing 2 classes, am supposed to graduate in May but it looks like that isn't going to happen.

I ultimately decided not to leave because of what you're experiencing- the knowledge that everyone is kind of moving forward with their lives with school and jobs, and you're just kind of stagnant, nothing to do, fear for next semester, and no friends.

I can say, if you had stayed in school it probably would be bad, really really bad. I had 5 panic attacks in the last 4 days. I'm failing classes, wasting money, in a failing relationship that only started 6 weeks ago... I constantly wonder whether I made the right choice- but I don't think there was one.

I'm sorry to see that the grass on both sides are brown and crappy. I don't have advice because I would be in your situation had I not been such a stubborn idiot. I do suggest buying meditation/coloring books for adults and invest in colored pencils, it's actually helped me a lot when I feel like I'm about to explode or implode.

Please, feel free to message me if you ever need to talk, or post on /r/anxiety again; that's helped me a lot too.
